Baidu’s Q1 2026 earnings conference call, held on May 18, 2026, highlighted a monumental shift in the company's operational identity. For the first time, AI-powered segments crossed the self-sustaining threshold, generating over half of Baidu Core's general business revenue.   While macroeconomic headwinds subtly pressured legacy search and online marketing, rapid enterprise AI cloud adoption and cost discipline allowed Baidu to deliver an unexpected bottom-line beat.

1. Financial Performance Overview  Total Revenue: Reached RMB 32.1 billion (~$4.54 billion), beating consensus expectations across the board despite a slight 2% dip quarter-over-quarter.    Baidu General Business Revenue: Clocked in at RMB 26.0 billion, flat quarter-over-quarter but up 2% year-over-year.  The AI Tipping Point: Core AI-powered business revenue hit RMB 13.6 billion, a massive 49% surge year-over-year. This segment now accounts for 52% of Baidu’s general business revenue.    Profitability & Leverage: Adjusted profit and operating profit both surpassed Wall Street forecasts, signaling that massive R&D and AI infrastructure spending is finally shifting from capital expense to strong operational leverage.   2. Segment & Operational Breakdown AI Cloud (The Primary Engine)  Revenue: Recorded RMB 8.8 billion, representing an explosive 79% year-over-year increase.    Drivers: Management credited China's aggressive domestic enterprise migration to large language models (LLMs).
